simulator_description: This simulator models COVID-like epidemic dynamics using a discrete-time stochastic SIR compartment model, generating trajectories of integer counts (S, I, R) over time under a fixed population size N. At each step it samples new infections as a binomial draw from susceptibles with an infection probability derived from a mass-action force of infection (1-exp(-beta*I/N)), and samples recoveries as a binomial draw from infecteds with probability gamma; it then enforces nonnegativity and exact conservation S+I+R=N, matching the data validation assumptions. Parameters (beta, gamma) are calibrated via simulation-based inference (NPE/SNPE) using a single observed training trajectory (trajectory_id=0), comparing flattened, population-scaled and z-scored trajectories with additional time/peak weighting to emphasize informative early and peak dynamics. After calibration, the simulator runs multiple stochastic rollouts per trajectory (with split RNG streams and per-rollout seeds for stability) and uses the mean rollout as the predicted trajectory for evaluation against train/val/test observations.
